messages:
Anya P: Quick sync — I'm sketching a proposal for the private-deploy packaging that aims to minimize NetOps changes customers must make. Two upgrade paths: (A) in-place rolling operator upgrade with compatibility shim, (B) parallel side-by-side operator + live traffic migration. Need concrete tradeoffs and installer UX expectations. thoughts?

Mike B: +1 on documenting both, but we should default to (B) for high-risk enterprise customers. In-place is faster but fragile w/ CNI/kernel differences.

Jordan R: (B) costs more infra and more DB/kv migration complexity. Can we design a staged-rolling that keeps the same IPs and mounts to avoid peering+DNS churn? customers really hate rekeying firewalls.

Sara L: Field datapoint — several finance customers requested "no additional open ports" airgap installer + zero IP churn. They prefer a predictable ~15min maintenance window vs long parallel migrations. Also KMS/HSM rotation story is a blocker.

deploy-bot: CI note: private-installer-e2e / canary-20240312 failed: CNI compatibility test flagged on Ubuntu22.04 (calico v3.25). Logs attached: https://ci.internal/reports/20240312/ci-234

NetOps T: If we go staged rolling and preserve IPs we need to guarantee no ephemeral host-network change. That implies we either implement an ip-preserve layer in the operator or rely on a sidecar bridge. Both have tradeoffs.

Liwei Z: Proposal: make the installer support three modes: `preserve-ips` (best-effort IP continuity), `parallel-migration` (spin new operator + migrate workloads), and `offline-shim` (airgap-friendly bundle for disconnected installs). Default = `preserve-ips` for small customers, `parallel-migration` opt-in for enterprise.

Anya P: Liwei — can you sketch the UX for toggling those modes during upgrade? We need clear warnings about downtime and an automated preflight that checks CNI compatibility, kernel modules, and KMS access.

Liwei Z: UX sketch (quick):
```yaml
# installer configuration fragment
installer:
  mode: preserve-ips            # preserve-ips | parallel-migration | offline-shim
  preflight:
    cni_compat: [calico, cilium]
    check_kms: true
    max_downtime_minutes: 15
  rollback_on_failure: true
```
Short CLI: `rw-installer upgrade --mode=preserve-ips --preflight` returns a list of riskiest checks and estimated window.

Mike B: We should add a network-policy overlay option so customers can opt into maintaining existing iptables rules rather than reprogramming them. Might require node-level daemonset perms.

Jordan R: Also add KV cache migration hooks in the operator: we can snapshot and warm the new operator so requests don't spike latency. That makes parallel route-switch much smoother.

Sara L: Launch criteria suggestion: 1) Preflight covers top 5 field failure modes, 2) Installer supports both preserve-ips and parallel-migration, 3) Docs + migration runbook, 4) One pilot customer completes migration with <2% request error spike.

Anya P: Agree on those gates. We also need a clear rollback plan: if parallel migration fails halfway, we must be able to route traffic back with no state loss. Jordan, can you own the migration/rollback playbook?

Jordan R: I can own it. I'll draft a playbook with state checkpointing and an emergency revert flag (operator sidecar listens for `revert=true`). Will include `kubectl` snippets and an automated smoke test.

NetOps T: For customers that insist on "no new peering" — we can support a NAT-based connector for outbound-only control-plane. That fits offline-shim use-case. Need to confirm with security on egress TLS inspection.

Anya P: Action items: Liwei — spec installer modes + CLI by EOD Fri. Jordan — migration/rollback draft by Wed. Mike/NetOps — short note on required node perms and ip-preserve daemonset by Thu. Sara — identify two pilot customers and own the field run. I'll collate into a concise launch checklist after those deliverables.

Mike B: I'll run a permissions matrix with minimal RBAC needed and post it to this thread.

Liwei Z: Quick FYI — offline-shim bundle will be ~120MB compressed when we strip debug symbols; need agreement on signing + checksum UX for airgapped installs.

Sara L: For pilots, prefer customers that already run Calico and have staging environments. I'll reach out today.

Anya P: Thanks all. If anyone spots missing acceptance criteria, add now. Otherwise I'll capture this thread into the roadmap ticket and create sub-tasks. :thumbsup:
